name: Responsive object grid
description: The second grid kind: placement led by the object, not the column. Children declare a minimum and maximum width and the row fits as many as will go, wrapping when they no longer fit. Will's note is the whole specification — 'object based min max lead (can be in or out of a container)' — and the distinction matters because a column grid cannot express 'as many cards as fit, at least 230px each'. Specified in Figma as Responsive-flex-Grid-8 with 120 instances on the layout page; no S2A implementation exists, so every rule here asserts absence and will flip when the CSS lands.

breakpointBehavior.behavior: Proposed: one or two per row depending on the declared minimum against a ~327px content width.
Proposed: as many as fit above the minimum; Will's working figure is a 230px floor.
Proposed: as many as fit, capped by the declared maximum so items do not stretch.
Proposed: the item count rises with the container rather than the items growing.

tokens.note: Figma names the system flex-Grid-8 after this 8px gutter.

classes.name: object-grid
classes.purpose: Proposed: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min, max)) row that wraps on the item's own minimum.

classes.name: object-min-230
classes.purpose: Proposed: the 230px floor Will records as covering the current mocks.

customProperties.name: --s2a-object-min
customProperties.purpose: Proposed: the item's minimum width, the value that decides when the row wraps.

customProperties.name: --s2a-object-max
customProperties.purpose: Proposed: the item's maximum width, so a lone item does not stretch across the container.

rules.statement: No object-grid class exists in S2A yet. This contract is the specification, and this rule is what keeps that honest.
No object minimum custom property exists yet.
The gutter token the system would use already ships, so the implementation needs no new tokens.
Figma's layout guide confirms the 8px gutter the name refers to.

decisions.question: What is the canonical object minimum — 230px, as Will's note says covers the mocks, or a token on the spacing scale?
decisions.evidence: Figma note: 'a min of 230 will cover mocks for now'. 230 is not on the spacing scale, which suggests either a new layout token or a rounded value such as 232 (29 × 8).

decisions.question: Will's note says an object grid can live inside or outside a container. If outside, what supplies its side margins?
decisions.evidence: '(can be in our out of a container)'. Outside a container there is no percentage rule and no token ladder, so an uncontained object grid would need its own margin rule or it bleeds to the viewport edge.

decisions.question: Does the object grid need the orphan behaviour the ups grid has, where a lone last item stretches?
decisions.evidence: Figma's note about the ups grid mentions 'can add orphan feature to last item of a set'. An auto-fit row leaves a lone item at its maximum width rather than stretching, which may already be the desired behaviour.

visualize.note: Rendered from the proposed rules with inline CSS so the behaviour is visible before the stylesheet exists. Labelled as a proposal, not a shipped class.
